Testimony of Meghan Russo Maine Department of Transportation
Before the 132"" Legislature, Joint Standing Committee on Transportation
Neither For Nor Against
LD 862, Resolve, to Honor Scarborough Veterans by Renaming the Pine Point Crossing
Bridge the Scarborough Veterans Memorial Bridge
Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts and distinguished members of the Joint Standing
Committee on Transportation, I am Meghan Russo, Director of Government Affairs at MaineDOT. MaineDOT is neither for nor against LD 862.
MaineDOT considers the naming of bridges, roadways, and other state transportation infrastructure to be within the purview of the Legislature. Simply put, we build them and you name them. Accordingly, we generally do not take positions on so-called "naming bills." However, we usually submit written testimony regarding whether the particular infrastructure under consideration has been named before, and if so what those name(s) are. In this case, we are not aware of any previous legislatively-sanctioned names for this bridge. MaineDOT's
current inventory number for this structure is 5260.
Thank you.

Testimony ofRepresentative Sophie Warren introducing
L.D. 862, Resolve, to Honor Scarborough Veterans by Renaming the Pine Point Crossing Bridge the Scarborough Veterans Memorial Bridge
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Transportation
Good aftemoon, Chair Nangle, Chair Crafts, and respected colleagues of the Joint
Standing Committee on Transportation. I appreciate the opportunity to present L.D. 862,
Resolve, to Honor Scarborough Veterans by Renaming the Pine Point Crossing Bridge the Scarborough Veterans Memorial Bridge.
This proposal represents a simple way to honor our Scarborough veterans, supported not
only by every legislator representing a part of our Scarborough community, but also endorsed
unanimously by our local Scarborough Town Council. Please see the letter attached from the Town Council attached to this testimony. '
Additionally,- I washeaitened by conversations in past weeks within my community
reflecting thoughtful support of this measure. During a recent meeting of the local Pine Point
Association, the part of my district most directly impacted by this bill, we discussed how this
crossing is the connecting point between the Pine Point region and the rest of our town, and what
it meant to make this change. Some had never realized the name of the bridge, while others who
did, understood it to be a great message to communicate through this change on behalf of the Pine Point community.
This bill is a part of a larger effort to honor our veterans by renaming several bridges
across our state in this way. There are so many ways our veterans deserve to see our state honor
them. I want to thank and credit my town's leadership in helping to bring our community into
these efforts in this way to do so. I also thank former Senate Chair of the Joint Standing Committee on Transportation, Benjamin Chipman and Calista Cross for their work in this effort
and echo our town's thanks for "[their] dedication to serving and recognizing our Veterans."
Thank you for your time and consideration of this bill. I would be happy to answer any
questions you may have.
